newsitem.title: USA: ISS backs Sallie Mae management.
newsitem.headline: ISS backs Sallie Mae management.

text.p: Institutional Shareholder Services (ISS), a firm which advises large institutional stockholders on how to vote in proxy contests, Monday recommended a vote for a reorganization plan proposed by the management of Student Loan Marketing Association (Sallie Mae).
ISS could not be reached for comment but a copy of the organization's 35-page report circulated through Wall Street Monday afternoon.
ISS said the business plan of the Sallie Mae management "is the more sensible choice" than that of the Committee to Restore Value (CRV), an opposition group.
ISS said it found the plan developed by Albert Lord, a former Sallie Mae executive who heads the CRV, "tempting and forward-looking" but lacking in specifics.

"We are not certain of the specifics regarding how Sallie Mae deftly but aggressively transitions from loan servicer to orginator within the CRV's projected time frame without a significant potential loss of loan purchase volume from customers who are likely to become competitors," ISS said.
The CRV has scheduled a vote on its proposals May 9, while the management has a meeting scheduled for May 15.

"It (the ISS report) will make some difference with certain investors," Lord said in telephone interview. "We're obviously very disappointed." He continued, "ISS made a caluclation that our business plan was riskier than the management's. We disagree with that obviously."

Lord said that the ISS report give his group "credit for influencing Sallie Mae's new focus on balance sheet management and greater emphasis on cost cutting." But he said ISS "condensed the issues" and made the votes a referendum on whether Sallie Mae should originate loans. Lord said he thought that focus was too narrow.
Lord noted that two Sallie Mae executives, vice president and treasurer Robert Levine and vice president and controller Mark Overend, have stated they will vote in favor of the CRV proposals.

Both the CRV and the management of Sallie Mae are sponsoring plans that would convert Sallie Mae from a government-sponsored enterprise to a a private corporation. The groups are running different slates of candidates for a new board. ISS's recommendations include voting in favor of the management slate of directors.
